source: Durian Orchard (ការដាំធូរេន), by Vann Thana Busab and Montry Vong Phanith, published by the Northwest Cambodia Provinces Fruit Culture Development Committee (Battambang), 1998, 59pp, AIDOC code 178-001
text:
During flowering, remove any flower clusters growing on very thin, weak branches or crowded close together on a single branch, keeping the more robust clusters spaced well apart so the tree channels its energy into fewer, stronger flower sets rather than an excessive, unsustainable flower load.

Durian flowers open in the evening and are primarily pollinated at night. The source describes a hand-pollination technique for growers who want to improve fruit set: collect ripe pollen from open flowers between about 7:00-7:30pm using a soft brush or cotton swab into a small container, then apply it by hand to the stigma of other open flowers between roughly 7:30-9:00pm the same evening, working systematically branch by branch. This hand-pollination is recommended particularly where natural pollinator activity (insects and, most importantly for durian, nectar-feeding bats) is thought to be low, since durian sets fruit poorly without adequate pollination.

Fertilizer during/just before flowering: apply a low-nitrogen, high-potassium formula such as 0-0-50 at 1-2kg per tree, timed about 7-8 days before expected fruit-set, to support the developing flowers and improve fruit quality rather than push vegetative growth.

If the flowering flush overlaps with a leaf-flush, thin out some of the new leaf shoots so the tree is not splitting its energy between vegetative growth and reproductive growth at the same critical window.
